messages:
jamie: hey @morgan — saw your support ticket about a 403 on the Billing > Usage page. can you paste the exact URL and when you hit it?

morgan: /orgs/oss-inc/billing/usage at 2024-11-02T15:12:02Z. I can open Project settings fine but billing throws 403. tried incognito, same.

leo: did you capture the network response? 403 vs 401 will tell us if it's auth vs permission.

morgan: network response body: {\"error\":\"forbidden\",\"reason\":\"missing_scope\",\"required\":\"billing:read\"}

anya: checking org config. user morgan@example.com is in org-role devops which should inherit billing:read via the group -> role mapping. note: we did a group rename in Okta last night.

scim-sync-bot: SCIM sync completed 2024-11-02T03:07:12Z. actions: group rename: infra-team -> infra-core; members updated: 4; custom attrs inspected.

jamie: can you replicate using the API to rule out console bug? e.g.:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/oss-inc/billing/usage
```

morgan: reproduced via curl, same 403. introspected token scopes:
```
{"scopes":["projects:read","models:invoke"]}
```
no billing scopes present.

leo: ok this screams SCIM attr loss. when we rename groups some IdPs strip custom group attributes unless mapping preserved. anya — can you dump the infra-core group attrs from IdP?

anya: verified. infra-core lacks `redwood:role=billing_admin` attribute that old infra-team had. the rename mapping in Okta didn't carry over custom group metadata.

jamie: root cause hypothesis: SCIM rename removed the custom role attribute, so the org-role mapping no longer includes billing:read, tokens issued post-sync don't include billing scope — hence 403.

leo: for a quick customer unblock there are a few options:
- restore the `redwood:role=billing_admin` attr on the group in IdP and resync SCIM (recommended)
- grant billing role directly to the user/org via the CLI or admin UI
- generate a short-lived org token for reports while we fix the IdP mapping

anya: i'm adding the attribute back in Okta now and will trigger a SCIM resync.

jamie: alternative CLI command that will assign a role immediately (admins only):
```
redwood org grant-role --org oss-inc --principal morgan@example.com --role billing_reader
```

morgan: ran the CLI command as suggested but still see 403. maybe the console caches role assertions or the session token hasn't been reissued.

leo: yep tokens are minted at login and cached on the client. try signing out of the console and sign in again or create a new API key from the API keys page. we'll also flush our role cache on the auth side in ~5 minutes.

scim-sync-bot: SCIM sync started 2024-11-02T15:34:01Z.

anya: SCIM resync finished. infra-core now shows `redwood:role=billing_admin` in group attrs.

morgan: signed out, cleared session, signed back in. billing page loads fine now :tada:

jamie: great — next steps recorded:
- Account Ops (anya): update Okta group rename/runbook to preserve custom attrs and validate mappings after rename.
- SRE (leo): consider lowering role-assertion cache TTL and add a short manual invalidate endpoint for emergency fixes.
- Support (jamie): confirm with customer and close the ticket once they confirm stability.

morgan: all good, thanks for the fast help!
